subject: AWS private offer: variable credit phasing and reseller margin tranching
messages:
From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@acme.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-05-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify private offer credit phasing + partner margin

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team loved the latency benchmarks. Procurement is working the internal approval and we have two items blocking sign-off on the private offer:

1) The crediting schedule in the draft shows a quarterly true-up — we need an option to front-load 30% of year-one credits in Q1 to match our budget runway. Can Redwood support a variable phasing (30/20/25/25) instead of equal quarters?

2) The reseller (Cloud Reseller) is requesting clarity on how their margin is tranching against the committed dollars. Their finance team wants a simple waterfall: reseller gets 10% on the first $200k of usage, 7% on the next $300k, then 4% thereafter. Will Redwood invoice net-of-reseller, or do we need to flow credits through a separate distributor settlement?

Attached the draft PO and a short table of the suggested phasing. Appreciate a consolidated answer — procurement needs it for the Monday exec review.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Miller
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation

Attachments: ACME_PO_terms_v1.pdf (pdf), phasing-table.png (image)
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@acme.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, irene_choi@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-05-18T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify private offer credit phasing + partner margin

Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the draft. Short answers up front: yes on variable phasing, and we can support reseller tranching but invoicing options depend on how you want margin routed. Details below.

1) Credit phasing: Redwood can set an accelerated credit schedule per the 30/20/25/25 profile. Operationally we implement that as front-loaded prepaid credits applied to the invoice cycle; unused credits after year 1 are eligible for pro-rated refunds only upon contract termination (we'll show the amortization schedule in the PO). We will send an updated PO PDF with the explicit schedule.

2) Reseller margin / invoice flow: two supported approaches — choose one:
  - Net-of-reseller (simpler for Acme): Redwood invoices Acme for net usage after reseller margin is applied. We pay the reseller separately via partner settlement. Requires reseller to accept netting in their reseller agreement.
  - Gross invoice + distributor settlement: Redwood invoices Acme the gross amount, and the reseller submits a settlement claim to Redwood/partner ops for reimbursement per the waterfall. This preserves gross revenue recognition for Acme but adds a reconciliation step quarterly.

I'll loop in Ben (finance) and Irene (partner ops) to confirm mechanics and any accounting constraints. We can produce both invoice samples to help your FP&A choose.

Next steps: Ben/Irene — can you confirm which flow you prefer from a revenue/settlement perspective? Sarah — if you confirm front-load phasing and the waterfall percentages, Ben will attach a sample amortization table and Irene will map the settlement path.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-private-offer-sku-mapping.xlsx (xlsx)
From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com, Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@acme.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-05-18T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify private offer credit phasing + partner margin

Quick finance note: for Acme's preference (front-load 30% Q1), revenue recognition will follow the credits usage pattern unless Acme elects prepayment accounting. If Acme wants the revenue to be recognized later while still receiving the Q1 benefit, we can structure a refund-triggered escrow (rare) but it complicates audits.

On the reseller tranching: Net-of-reseller is cleaner from a settlement standpoint for Redwood and reduces quarterly reconciliation, but it requires the reseller to accept a netting clause in their reseller agreement. If the reseller insists on gross invoice + settlement, we'll need a quarterly reconciliation report (we can auto-generate) and a short SLA for claim window (60 days).

I've attached a sample amortization table and an illustrative invoice (sample rows) — see column "Effective Net After Reseller" which shows how the waterfall reduces our collected gross.

Ben
Ben Carter
Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: sample-amortization.csv (csv)
From: irene_choi@redwood.example.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@acme.com>, partners@cloud-reseller.com
Date: 2026-05-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify private offer credit phasing + partner margin

Adding partner ops detail and the expected operational steps if Acme picks gross invoice + settlement: 

- We will create a partner settlement account for Cloud Reseller. They must be onboarded (W-9 / tax forms completed).
- Each invoice, Redwood will include an attachment with the waterfall calculation and a claim ID. The reseller will submit claims via our partner portal.
- Quarterly reconciliation: Redwood produces an "Invoices vs Settlements" CSV and pays cleared claims on a Net-30 after approval. We require claims to be submitted within 60 days of invoice date or they expire.

If Acme signs up for net-of-reseller: we will need the reseller to sign the netting addendum. That removes the claims flow; Redwood will remit the reseller fee on our settlement cadence.

Jordan — can you confirm the onboarding checklist and expected lead time for Cloud Reseller? Sarah — can you confirm which invoice flow procurement prefers so we can finalize the PO?

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Partner Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify private offer credit phasing + partner margin

Irene — onboarding checklist below (we'll start as soon as we have reseller contact + signed MSA addendum):

1) Reseller registration (legal/tax docs): 5 business days once submitted.
2) Bank details + remit account: 2 business days.
3) Partner portal access + claim template: 3 business days.
4) Test settlement run (dry run): optional, 4 business days.

Operational recommendation for Acme: choose net-of-reseller if you want minimal reconciliation overhead. If Cloud Reseller requires gross invoice treatment, choose the gross invoice path but we suggest adding a 60-day claim window and automated settlement to reduce friction.

Sarah — if you confirm (a) front-loaded phasing 30/20/25/25 and (b) net-of-reseller invoicing, we will:
  - produce an updated PO with explicit amortization schedule,
  - attach sample net invoices for your FP&A, and
  - prepare the netting addendum for Cloud Reseller to sign.

Sent from Jordan Blake (Deal Desk) — happy to run the sample invoice with your CFO in a quick call.

--
Jordan Blake
Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
